Moves & help
Your moves will appear here. Try a ring or press Randomize.

Every ring turn is a legal cube move.

How to play & keyboard shortcuts

The pieces keep their dimensions as you turn them. Restore the original cube shape to solve it.

This is a Mirror Cube, also known as Mirror Blocks. It follows 3×3 cube moves with off-center layer cuts and differently sized pieces. Every piece is rigid: turning layers rearranges the blocks into new shapes. The goal is to restore the smooth cube.

Select a ring with its letter button or exposed arc, then use either turn arrow. Drag along its curve and release for one 90° step. Drag the 3D puzzle to look around; scroll or pinch to zoom.

The ring map tracks all 54 surface stickers as uniform solid-color dots. Turn on “Mirror mode” in the 3D view for an advanced shape-only challenge: the puzzle becomes silver and the ring map disappears. Notation moves remain below the larger 3D view. Switching modes preserves your puzzle, move history and camera.

Use ←/→ for the selected ring. U D L R F B M E S make standard moves; hold Shift for inverse. A prime (′) means inverse, and 2 means a half-turn. With the 3D view focused, arrow keys change the camera and +/− zoom.

Randomize continues from the current position and applies 24 seeded legal turns. Every click creates a fresh seed. Auto solve opens the Constrained Solver and works from the current arrangement, pausing between stages and highlighting solved nodes that later stages protect. It does not need recorded moves or promise the shortest solution; difficult states may reach the computation limit. This standalone game works offline.
